Fit the Bayesian Efron log-spline model to estimates and standard errors

Source: R/fit.R
bayes_efron_fit.Rd

A meta-analysis or a multisite trial gives an estimate \(\hat\theta_i\) and a standard error \(\sigma_i\) for each of \(K\) sites. bayes_efron_fit() treats the true effects \(\theta_i\) as draws from an unknown distribution \(g\) and estimates \(g\) and each \(\theta_i\) together. Unlike the usual random-effects model, it does not assume that \(g\) is normal: \(g\) can be skewed or have more than one peak, and the amount of shrinkage for each estimate depends on that shape.

The result contains posterior draws of \(g\). Functions such as site_summary(), g_summary() and plot() compute posterior means, intervals and probabilities for the sites and for \(g\) from these draws.

The model is fitted by Markov chain Monte Carlo with CmdStan, so the cmdstanr package and CmdStan must be installed. The first call compiles the Stan program, which can take up to a minute. Later calls reuse the compiled model (see bayes_efron_compile()).

Usage

bayes_efron_fit(
  theta_hat,
  sigma = NULL,
  ...,
  grid = NULL,
  grid_method = "pilot",
  support = NULL,
  L = NULL,
  expansion = 0.5,
  margin = 0.1,
  M = 6L,
  knots = "grid",
  component = c("point", "normal"),
  width = 2/3,
  theta_true = NULL,
  bound_expansion = NULL,
  settings = NULL,
  model_family = "RE",
  chains = 4L,
  parallel_chains = chains,
  iter_warmup = 1000L,
  iter_sampling = 3000L,
  adapt_delta = 0.9,
  max_treedepth = 10L,
  seed = NULL,
  keep_cmdstan_fit = FALSE,
  store_grid_quantities = FALSE,
  site_draws = FALSE,
  thin = 1L,
  refresh = NULL,
  init = 0.5,
  show_messages = NULL
)

Arguments

theta_hat

Numeric vector of effect estimates, one per site, all on the same scale (e.g., standardized mean differences or log odds ratios). Names, if present, are used as site labels. Can also be a data frame or a bef_data object that contains the estimates and their standard errors (see as_bef_data()), in which case sigma is omitted. At least 5 sites are required.

sigma

Numeric vector of standard errors of the estimates, the same length as theta_hat. All must be positive.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

grid

A bef_grid object created by make_efron_grid(). If NULL (the default), the grid is built from the arguments that follow. If a grid is supplied, grid_method, support, L, expansion, margin, M, knots, component, width, theta_true and bound_expansion must not be specified.

grid_method

Method for choosing the limits of the grid: "pilot" (the default), "paper_realdata", "paper_simulation" or "paper_sensitivity". See the Details of make_efron_grid(). With "pilot", the pilot fit uses this call's seed and parallel_chains, so the grid is the same as the one returned by make_efron_grid() with that seed.

support

Numeric vector of length 2 with the lower and upper limits of the grid. If NULL (the default), the limits are chosen by grid_method.

L

Number of grid points, an integer from 51 to 401. If NULL (the default), the number is chosen from the data: 101, or more if 101 points are too few for the standard errors or for the spread of the effects. See the Details of make_efron_grid().

expansion

Expansion factor, a number between 0 and 5. With grid_method = "pilot" or "paper_realdata", the range of theta_hat is extended on each side by expansion times its width.

margin

Margin for grid_method = "pilot", a number between 0 and 1. The interval that contains the central 99.9% of the pilot estimate of \(g\) is extended on each side by margin times its width.

M

Number of spline functions, an integer from 3 to 10. More spline functions allow \(g\) to have narrower features. In simulated data sets of 1,500 sites, the site intervals contained somewhat fewer of the true effects with 8 functions than with 6 (see vignette("twin-towers")).

knots

Method for placing the knots of the spline functions. Currently only "grid" is available; see the Details of make_efron_grid().

component

Type of component at each grid point: "point" (the default) for a point mass, or "normal" for a normal distribution.

width

Standard deviation of the normal components in units of the grid spacing, a number greater than 0 and at most 2. Only used with component = "normal".

theta_true

Numeric vector of true effects, the same length as theta_hat. Required by "paper_simulation" and "paper_sensitivity", which are intended for simulations.

bound_expansion

Expansion factor for grid_method = "paper_sensitivity", a number greater than 0 and at most 5: the range of theta_true is extended on each side by bound_expansion times its width. NULL (the default) is equivalent to 0.5.

settings

Set to "0.3.0" to fit the model as version 0.3.0 of the package did. The fit then uses that version's Stan program and its defaults for grid_method ("paper_realdata"), L (101) and site_draws (TRUE); arguments that you set yourself are kept. With NULL (the default), the same seed gives different draws than it did in version 0.3.0, and a message about the changed defaults is shown once per session. See vignette("implementation") for when the draws of version 0.3.0 are reproduced exactly.

model_family

Model family. Currently only "RE", the model described in Details, is available.

chains

Number of Markov chains, an integer from 1 to 16.

parallel_chains

Number of chains to run in parallel, an integer from 1 to chains. By default all chains run in parallel.

iter_warmup

Number of warmup iterations per chain.

iter_sampling

Number of sampling (post-warmup) iterations per chain, at least 1.

adapt_delta

Target acceptance rate of the sampler, a number between 0 and 1. A higher value leads to a smaller step size, which can remove divergent transitions but makes sampling slower. With about 20 sites, divergent transitions are common with the default of 0.9, and 0.99 is a better starting value (see vignette("teacher-expectancy")).

max_treedepth

Maximum tree depth of the sampler, an integer from 1 to 20. Increase it if diagnose() reports many iterations that reached the maximum.

seed

Integer seed for the sampler. If NULL (the default), a seed is taken from the clock. In either case the seed that was used is stored in the result.

keep_cmdstan_fit

If TRUE, the cmdstanr::CmdStanMCMC object is stored in the result as cmdstan_fit. It refers to temporary files, so it is only useful in the session that created it.

store_grid_quantities

If TRUE, the draws also include the grid probabilities g and their unnormalized logarithms log_w, which adds 2 * L variables. This is not needed for the methods, which compute both from the other draws.

site_draws

If TRUE, the fit also stores five variables per site (theta_mean, theta_sd, theta_map, theta_rep and log_lik), which confint(method = "draws") requires. If FALSE (the default, except with settings = "0.3.0"), only the draws of the parameters and of \(g\) are stored, and all site summaries are computed from them when they are requested. Both choices give the same draws of \(g\) for the same seed.

thin

Thinning interval, an integer from 1 to iter_sampling. From each chain, one iteration out of every thin is stored, starting with the first. Thinning reduces the size of the result. It does not affect the sampler diagnostics reported by diagnose() (e.g., R-hat and the effective sample sizes), which are computed from all iterations. The summaries and the grid diagnostics are computed from the stored draws.

refresh

Number of iterations between progress updates from CmdStan; 0 turns them off. If NULL (the default), 200 is used in an interactive session and 0 otherwise.

init

Initial values for the chains. A number x (default 0.5) draws the initial values uniformly between -x and x on the unconstrained scale, i.e., for the spline coefficients and for the logarithm of the precision. The default is narrower than CmdStan's default of 2. Can also be a list with one list of values of alpha and lambda per chain, or a function that returns such a list of values.

show_messages

If TRUE, the output of CmdStan and the messages of cmdstanr about the sampler are shown. If NULL (the default), they are shown in an interactive session only. The package's own warnings and diagnose() do not depend on this argument.

Value

An object of class c("bef_fit_re", "bef_fit"), which is a list with the following components.

draws

The posterior draws, a posterior::draws_array.

posterior

A list with the draws of the mean, the variance and the standard deviation of \(g\), of effective_params and of log_marginal_likelihood.

metadata

A list with the data, the settings and summaries of the draws.

cmdstan_fit

The cmdstanr::CmdStanMCMC object, only with keep_cmdstan_fit = TRUE.

See bef_fit for the details of these components and for the available methods.

Details

The model for sites \(i = 1, \ldots, K\) is $$\hat\theta_i \mid \theta_i \sim N(\theta_i, \sigma_i^2), \qquad \theta_i \sim g.$$ The standard errors \(\sigma_i\) are treated as known and may differ between sites. The distribution \(g\) has probabilities \(g_1, \ldots, g_L\) on a grid of points \(\tau_1 < \cdots < \tau_L\), with $$\log g_j = B_j^\top \alpha - \log \sum_{l=1}^{L} \exp(B_l^\top \alpha),$$ where \(B_j\) is the vector of values of the \(M\) natural cubic spline functions at \(\tau_j\). This is the log-spline family of Efron (2016). The coefficients have independent priors \(\alpha_m \mid \lambda \sim N(0, 1/\lambda)\), which pull \(g\) toward the uniform distribution on the grid. The precision has the prior \(\lambda \sim \mbox{half-Cauchy}(0, 5)\), so the strength of that pull is estimated along with the coefficients. See Lee and Sui (2025) for the model and for a comparison with the empirical Bayes estimator, in which \(\alpha\) is fixed at an estimate. With component = "normal", each grid point carries a normal distribution instead of a point mass, all with the same standard deviation, and \(g\) is their mixture with weights \(g_j\).

The grid and the spline basis are built as in make_efron_grid(), which describes the arguments that control them: grid_method or support for the range, L for the number of points, component and width for what is placed at each point, and M and knots for the spline functions. Alternatively, a grid built in advance can be supplied as grid, in which case the other grid arguments must be omitted.

With the default grid_method = "pilot", the range is chosen in two steps. A short preliminary fit, the pilot fit, is run on the range of "paper_realdata", that is, the range of the estimates extended on each side by expansion times its width. With the default expansion this is the range used in the code that accompanies Lee and Sui (2025). The range is then narrowed to the region where the pilot fit places \(g\). It is never made wider than the initial range, and for some data, e.g., raudenbush1985 and krw_discrimination, it is not narrowed at all. See vignette("choosing-a-grid") for a discussion of these choices.

Only \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\) are sampled. Given \(\alpha\), the posterior distribution of each \(\theta_i\) has a closed form, and functions such as site_summary() compute it from the draws of \(g\). The fitted object stores those draws as one variable per grid point, so its size grows with L. With the default of 12,000 draws it takes about 12 MB of memory for 101 grid points and about 40 MB for 401.

To make a fit reproducible, specify seed. With the same seed, data and settings, the draws are the same on the same machine with the same versions of the packages and of CmdStan. The seed and the sampler settings are stored in the result (see bef_fit).

A warning is issued if there are divergent transitions, or if an R-hat value exceeds 1.05 (for fits with at least 400 draws in total). A warning is also issued if a quantity is constant within each chain but differs between chains, so that its R-hat is infinite. Use diagnose() to see all the diagnostics.

References

Efron, B. (2016). Empirical Bayes deconvolution estimates. Biometrika, 103(1), 1-20. doi:10.1093/biomet/asv068

Lee, J. and Sui, D. (2025). Fully Bayesian inference for meta-analytic deconvolution using Efron's log-spline prior. Mathematics, 13(16), 2639. doi:10.3390/math13162639

See also

as_bef_data(), make_efron_grid(), bef_fit, diagnose(), plot.bef_fit_re(), vignette("bayesEfron")

Examples

# Estimates and standard errors as two vectors. The call needs CmdStan.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- bayes_efron_fit(
  theta_hat = krw_discrimination$yi,
  sigma = krw_discrimination$sei,
  seed = 20250807
)

# The call that made `krw_fit`: the firms' names as site labels, and
# the draws thinned to every 15th.
dat <- as_bef_data(krw_discrimination, site = "firm_name")
fit <- bayes_efron_fit(dat, seed = 20250807, thin = 15)
} # }

# The stored result of the second call.
fit <- krw_fit
fit
#> <bayesEfron fit>
#> Model family: RE
#> Sites: 97
#> Grid method: pilot
#> Runtime: 0.7197 sec
#> Draws: 800 (4 chains, one iteration in 15 kept); site-level draws not kept
#> Diagnostics: Rhat 1.002; ESS bulk 1731; ESS tail 1780; divergences 0; treedepth hits 0
#> Standard errors: 0.005344 to 0.0392 (largest / smallest 7.335)
#> Grid: 101 points from -0.0829 to 0.1585; smallest standard error 2.213 grid spacings
#> Grid range: rule "pilot", not narrowed (the range of "paper_realdata"); point masses; 6 spline functions
#> Next: summary() and site_summary() for the sites, g_summary() for the distribution of effects, plot().
summary(fit)$prior_summary
#> $mean
#> [1] 0.01660178
#> 
#> $var
#> [1] 0.0003076948
#> 
#> $sd
#> [1] 0.01716216
#> 
confint(fit, parm = c(29, 65))
#> 90% posterior intervals (equal-tailed)
#>                   site         mean         lower       upper        point
#> Quest Diagnostics   29 -0.004794688 -0.0132080742 0.003356499 -0.004794688
#> Walmart             65  0.023868227  0.0004493205 0.055232668  0.023868227
plot(fit, type = "g")
